ns2:section.sectionText: "This version of Intro to Fiction will look at our contemporary investment in adaptation, and consider what we do when we revisit premodern texts in our current moment. Together we will explore a series of foundational myths and stories of the western canon, including The Iliad, Beowulf, Hamlet, and Cinderella, to consider how we use, adapt, transform, co-opt, revise, and critique those texts, their contexts, plots, characters, styles, affordances, and limitations, to serve contemporary investments and interpretations. Adaptation can reveal new perspectives on the originals, and their place in our collective imagination, as well as on ourselves, the world we live in, and the cultural touchstones we’ve inherited. [Course Texts: Madeline Miller’sThe Song of Achilles, Sarah Ruhl’s Eurydice, Marvel’s Thor: Ragnarok, Maria Dahvana Headley The Mere Wife, Cat Winters’ The Steep and Thorny Way, Malindo Lo’s Ash]"
